title: One Ticket, 800 Years

plan.narration: Sit down, traveller. One ticket, and my whole long story. I am the city you are riding into.
plan.image_prompt: A dark underground metro platform in the old city at night: a sleek metro train arriving with warm gold-lit windows, amber platform lamps reflecting on the polished floor, beyond the platform edge a suggestion of domes, minarets and bazaar rooftops in deep indigo silhouette, a faint teal glow of a distant river, wide 16:9 composition with the train's front near the centre, low warm lamplight and deep shadow, no people. Warm painterly illustration in the manner of Indian miniature painting and old Delhi lithographs: rich ochre, indigo and gold leaf, fine brushwork, soft lamplight and dusk glow, aged-paper warmth. plan.narration: The bazaar smells of frying and spice. Shah Jahan founded this capital in 1639; the Red Fort straddles this bazaar's eastern fringe.
Shah Jahan's daughter Jahanara laid out this street with its canal and moonlit pool. Tradition says the pool named Chandni Chowk.

plan.narration: Next, Chawri Bazaar. Above the stalls stands the Jama Masjid, finished in 1656 by about five thousand workers.

landmark.image_prompt: Jama Masjid, Delhi, at night seen from the foot of the hill it stands on: a broad red sandstone mosque with white marble inlay, raised on a tall stone plinth of wide stairways, three marble domes with golden finials, and two tall minarets striped in red sandstone and white marble, each crowned by a marble chhatri, flanking the great eastern gate. The square courtyard glows with lamplight from rows of small lanterns, a rectangular marble ablution tank pale at its centre, corner chhatris above the arcades. Deep indigo night sky, thin crescent moon, warm amber lamplight washing the sandstone, a few small distant figures climbing the stairs. plan.narration: Still forward in time. At Patel Chowk, Jantar Mantar: an observatory of instruments for measuring the heavens, finished in 1724.

landmark.image_prompt: Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, at night: an observatory of stone instruments on a low rise. At the centre rises ONE huge right-triangular sundial, the Samrat Yantra: a single tall wedge of masonry seen side-on, one long straight staircase climbing its sloping hypotenuse to a small platform at the top, and one broad graduated quadrant arc curving down on each side of the wedge (a single triangle only, nothing crossing it). It is flanked by two open-topped cylindrical masonry instruments with slanted inner scales and a pair of hollow hemispherical bowls cut with concentric arcs. All the instruments are plastered in deep terracotta-red lime with crisp white-lined edges and scales. Warm lamplight from low lanterns at the base grazes the red plaster; the graduated arcs climb into a deep indigo sky with a thin crescent moon and first stars. Wide 16:9, the great triangle near the horizontal centre, calm open sky in both upper corners, dark raked gravel and low parapets simple in the bottom fifth. Only two or three tiny distant turned-away figures for scale; quiet, reverent, warm mood. Warm painterly illustration in the manner of Indian miniature painting and old Delhi lithographs: rich ochre, indigo and gold leaf, fine brushwork, soft lamplight and dusk glow, aged-paper warmth. plan.narration: Forward, now. In 1931 the Viceroy inaugurated this capital. Tens of thousands of labourers raised the Viceroy's House, now Rashtrapati Bhavan.

Warm lamplight in the arcades and along the terrace, deep indigo dusk sky with the last amber light on the dome, dark green lawns and long shadows in the foreground. Wide 16:9, the dome and column near the horizontal centre, calm open sky in the upper corners, the lawn plain and simple in the bottom fifth. Qutb Minar was begun around 1199 by Qutb ud-Din Aibak and finished by Iltutmish, who made Delhi his capital.

landmark.image_prompt: Qutb Minar, Delhi, in early-morning golden light seen from inside the cloister courtyard of the Qutb complex: a tapering five-storey tower of red and grey sandstone, its shaft fluted with carved bands and stalactite bracketing, projecting balconies carried on muqarnas corbels between the storeys, rising from a low circular plinth banded with carved ornament. Soft pale-gold sky, long morning shadows across worn stone paving, warm haze over trimmed lawn and the low ruins of the surrounding complex, a few small distant figures at the tower's foot. Wide 16:9, the tower's shaft near the horizontal centre, pale open sky calm in both upper corners, plain paving simple in the bottom fifth. Quiet reverent morning mood. plan.narration: And beside it, an iron pillar from the 5th century that resists rust. Phosphorus is the secret.

landmark.image_prompt: The iron pillar of Delhi in the Qutb complex, seen close in early-morning golden light: a dark iron column about seven metres tall with a smooth fluted shaft and a spreading bell-pattern capital, standing on a low stone base on the paved courtyard, its blackened metal catching a warm rim of sunlight. Behind it the arcades and broken sandstone walls of the complex recede, with clipped grass and low garden walls; long soft shadows fall across the paving, pale gold sky and morning haze above. Wide 16:9, the pillar near the horizontal centre and filling most of the frame vertically, calm open sky in the upper corners, plain paving simple in the bottom fifth.
